description: The canonical role -> capability table for OFFLINE Shared Workspaces. It is a different scope from the Real-time table AUB publishes as `aub-collaboration-roles/1.0` (internal/membership/capability.go): the four role NAMES are the same four names, and nothing else about the two tables is shared. A Real-time capability is what a participant may do inside one AUC session; an Offline capability is what a member may do inside one durable AUB workspace. Two scopes, two vocabularies, two versions — so that adding an Offline capability cannot silently widen a Real-time session, and so that a component holding one table can say which question it is answering.

roles.summary: The workspace owner. Administers membership, roles, visibility and deletion, and is the only role that may detach an existing asset. Owns the workspace object, not the assets in it.
A trusted collaborator. Edits and saves existing assets, contributes new ones, annotates and resolves, and may ask an incumbent editor to escalate a collision to Real-time. Administers nothing.

A contributor. May upload and import NEW assets and may annotate and reply, and may not edit or save an asset that already exists. This is the whole point of the role: contribution without write access to somebody else's finished work.
Read-only, and the role a public joiner enters as. Views, downloads and reads annotations; writes nothing.

capabilities.summary: Read workspace metadata: name, description, visibility, owner, members and their roles, assets and their owners.
Read the workspace activity record — who did what, to which asset or member, when.
Change name, description and max_members. Uses the workspace metadata revision as its write precondition.
Change the workspace between public and private, subject to the asset-visibility invariant.
Delete the workspace.
Create a private, role-bearing, single-use invitation for a known account.
Change another member's workspace role.
Remove another member, which detaches every asset that member owns.
Leave the workspace voluntarily, which detaches every asset the leaver owns. NOT held by the Overlord: an owner who left would leave the workspace ownerless, and V1 has no ownership transfer.
Ask the Overlord for a higher role, with an optional bounded plain-text message. NOT held by the Overlord, who has nothing above them to request.
Approve or deny a pending role request.
See and open the workspace's assets that this membership grants access to.
Download an accessible asset.
Upload a NEW asset into the workspace. The uploader owns it and is charged its storage.
Attach an asset the caller already owns elsewhere. Ownership and storage accounting do not change.

Acquire the exclusive Offline edit lease on an EXISTING mutable asset. Holding the lease is not the same as being allowed to save; asset.save is the separate authority, exactly as the Real-time table separates map.write from map.save.
Commit a new durable revision of an existing asset. Always additionally gated by the lease, the revision CAS and the ASSET OWNER's storage state, never by the saver's.
Remove an existing asset from the workspace. Detaching never deletes the asset, never transfers ownership and never moves the storage charge.
Read workspace annotation threads and replies.
Create annotation threads and post replies.
Resolve and reopen an annotation thread. Knight deliberately does not hold it: a contributor may raise a point and may not declare it settled.

Ask the incumbent Offline editor of a blocked map to escalate it into a Real-time session. Held only by roles that could have edited the map, because a member who may not edit is directed to the role-upgrade path instead of using Real-time as a permission bypass.

Accept such a request and become the linked session's Overlord. Always additionally gated by actually holding the valid Offline lease on that asset; the capability is the role half of the question only.

non_nesting.why: The Overlord may not leave. Until workspace ownership transfer exists, an Overlord's only exits are to keep the workspace or delete it, so `leave` is the one capability the most privileged role does not hold.
There is no role above Overlord to request, and a workspace cannot be requested by asking for it.

asset.edit: no other valid lease on the asset
asset not in a linked Real-time session
asset.save: caller holds the valid lease for this client instance
asset owner's storage accepts the write
asset.detach: asset is not offline_editing, realtime_starting or realtime_active
asset is not a pinned dependency of an active edit or session
escalation.accept: caller holds the valid lease on the asset
asset is not already in a linked Real-time session
member.remove: target is not the workspace owner
no asset the target owns is a pinned dependency of active work
member.leave: caller is not the workspace owner
no asset the caller owns is a pinned dependency of active work
member.role.change: target is not the workspace owner
target holds no active lease when the change removes asset.edit
workspace.visibility.change: private -> public requires every attached asset to be public
workspace.delete: no asset in the workspace is offline_editing, realtime_starting or realtime_active
